specs.v: Do not jump or climb glass

description.html: Dubia roaches are the staple of most insect-eating lizards' diets. They are high in protein and have a soft body, so both babies and adults digest them easily. Unlike crickets, they do not chirp, jump, climb smooth surfaces or smell bad, which makes them practical to keep at home.

description.text: Sizes and which animals they suit

description.html: Small (nymphs) are for baby bearded dragons, leopard geckos and smaller lizards. Medium suit juveniles, and large are for bigger lizards and adult bearded dragons. Rule of thumb: the insect should not be wider than the space between the animal's eyes.

Keep them in a ventilated plastic box with egg cartons, in a warm, dry place. Feed them vegetables, fruit and dry food, because whatever the roaches eat ends up in your lizard. Dust them with calcium before feeding, and occasionally with a multivitamin. See how to combine different live foods on our lizard food page.
